Hi Marta — added technical detail below and attached a simplified queueing diagram (redwood-queueing-diagram.png). I've kept the language non-legal so you can paste into your SOW.

Operational summary (for contract/SOW):
1) Scope & baseline
   - Dedicated pool: N reserved GPUs (instance class: RDX-A100-40GB). SLO baseline defined at 2,000-token requests, 1 concurrent request per client session.
2) Latency commitment
   - Measured metric: end-to-end token-generation latency (request received -> final token emitted) at 95/99/99.9 percentiles across the pool.
   - Example: for a 4-node pool (16 gpus), measured in our benchmarks: P99 latency = 180ms, P99.9 = 320ms at 2K tokens and steady-state mixed QPS of 400 rps (small/large mix: 60/40).
   - Contract language suggestion: "Redwood will use commercially reasonable efforts to maintain P99.9 latency <= 350ms for the configured instance class under steady-state QPS as specified in Section X. Latency SLOs exclude scheduled maintenance windows, emergency mitigations, and customer-initiated workload misconfigurations."
3) Queueing & KV cache behavior
   - We operate continuous batching plus an adaptive KV cache with LRU eviction. Small-token bursts can increase batching overhead and evictions; to mitigate, we offer an "inflight-concurrency shield" configuration that reserves a portion of pool concurrency for long-running/large-token requests.
   - Example configuration: reserve 25% of total concurrency for large-token workloads; this reduces P99.9 variance by ~40% in our internal tests during small-token spikes.
4) Carveouts & maintenance windows
   - Standard: weekly maintenance window (60 min, scheduled between 02:00-05:00 local) with 7-day notice; quarterly extended maintenance (up to 4 hours) with 14-day notice.
   - Contractable exception: customers may opt into a "managed retrain window" carveout (e.g., nightly 90-min retrain) that is explicitly excluded from availability calculations if pre-scheduled and agreed in the SOW.
5) Remedy & credits
   - SLA credits apply for unplanned availability degradations outside carveouts. For latency SLO misses, we propose a token-based credit schedule (e.g., 5% monthly usage credit for two separate P99.9 misses in a billing cycle).

Attachment: redwood-queueing-diagram.png (shows request flow, KV cache lanes, reserved concurrency lane).

Great questions — summary and next steps below so procurement has a compact packet to review.

Summary points for SOW / procurement packet:
- Steady-state QPS definition: "Steady-state QPS" means the 5-minute moving average request rate observed over the first 10 business days after go-live, normalized to per-second (e.g., sustained 1200 rps). Parties may agree a different baseline measured over an onboarding window; any deviation must be captured in Section X.
- Managed retrain carveout + inflight-concurrency shield: Redwood will implement a reserved headroom lane (configurable, default 10% of pool concurrency; can be increased to 25% on request) that will not be preempted by internal preemption. Suggested SOW clause: "Redwood will reserve a dedicated concurrency lane ("Shield") equal to 10% of configured pool concurrency during customer-declared retrain windows. The Shield shall not be used for non-customer traffic or internal remediation events and shall be excluded from preemption policies, except for emergency security mitigations with 4-hour notice."
- Measurement & remedies: include the P99/P99.9 measurement windows, carveout exclusion rules, and the token-credit schedule for missed latency SLOs (as Laura outlined).
